title: TypeScript SDK: incremental type-gen and Zod adapters for partial/streaming structured outputs
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: Background: The TypeScript SDK currently emits a single, full-output type for structured output contracts. This breaks ergonomics for streaming scenarios where LLMs incrementally emit partial objects (fields or array chunks). Goal: produce incremental type generation and runtime Zod/JSON-schema helpers that make it easy for app authors to validate partial/streaming chunks and to compose them into the final shaped output.
proposal: 1) Add an incremental typegen mode: - `--incremental` flag for the codegen that emits helper types: `PartialStream<MainSchema>`, `Chunk<T>`, `Accumulated<T>` and utility overloads for async iterables. - Types should be additive (support merging object shards and appending array chunks) and preserve discriminated union narrowing across partials. 2) Runtime helpers: - `zod.streamPiece(schema)` which returns a Zod schema for validating a single chunk. - `zod.accumulator(schema)` which validates and reduces stream pieces to the final shape and throws on irreconcilable merges. 3) SDK API ergonomics: - New client overloads: `client.generateStructured<T>(opts): AsyncIterable<Chunk<T>>` and `client.collectStructured<T>(opts): Promise<T>` (collect uses accumulator). - Provide example: incremental parse in React streaming UI without forcing full JSON rebinding on every chunk. 4) Migration: - Old generated types remain compatible; incremental mode is opt-in. - Provide codemod snippets and docs page with examples and traps.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: - Safety vs ergonomics: relaxed merging rules increase developer convenience but may accept incorrect final outputs; accumulator will have a strict and permissive mode. - Complexity: adding incremental typegen increases surface area of generated types and nightly build times. We'll gate by flag to keep CI impact minimal. - Runtime perf: validating every chunk adds CPU; will add a caching strategy and allow disabling validation per-stream. - Discriminated unions: maintaining correct runtime narrowing across shards is non-trivial; plan to introduce a deterministic conflict resolution and tests across shards that include discriminators early in the stream.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): spec + PoC - Design precise shape of emitted helper types and zod helpers - PoC generator that emits incremental types for a small schema set - Implement `zod.streamPiece` and `zod.accumulator` helpers - Internal integration test harness with synthetic streaming sequences Phase 2 (1 sprint): SDK surface and docs - Add client overloads, examples in examples/streaming-incremental, and a migration guide - Benchmarks for validation overhead Phase 3 (1 sprint): polish - Codemods, more comprehensive union tests, add permissive/strict accumulator modes, and final review
acceptance_criteria: Generated types include PartialStream<...>, Chunk<...> and Accumulated<...> when --incremental is enabled
Zod helpers validate single chunks and can compose to final schema in both strict and permissive modes
client.generateStructured returns AsyncIterable of chunk types usable without unsafe casts
Integration tests cover object shard merges, array chunk append, and discriminated union narrowing across shards
Performance benchmark: validation adds <15% CPU overhead for common payload sizes with caching enabled
Migration guide and 3 examples: simple object, streaming array, and discriminated-union case

2025-02-25: Design review notes: PM requests clearer migration story; UX wants example for React Suspense streaming. Added to docs scope.
